title: git switch
definition: A newer command introduced in Git 2.23 explicitly designed to switch branches, resolving the confusing dual-nature of `git checkout`.
simpleExplanation: The modern, safer version of `git checkout`. It does exactly one thing: it switches branches. It cannot accidentally delete your files.
realWorldExample: You want to go to the `dev` branch. Instead of typing `git checkout dev`, you type `git switch dev`.

basic: What is the `git switch` equivalent of `git checkout -b` (create and switch)?
intermediate: If `git switch` is better, why do people still use `git checkout`?

answers.question: Why still use checkout?
answers.answer: Muscle memory. `git checkout` has been used for over a decade. Millions of tutorials and senior developers still use it automatically.

terminalOutput:
# Switch to an existing branch
$ git switch main

# CREATE and SWITCH to a new branch
$ git switch -c feature/payment-gateway

# Quickly switch back to the branch you were just on previously (like a TV remote 'Last Channel' button)
$ git switch -
